title: Screenshots, video and traces for diagnosing a failure

videos.script: A test fails on a build server at night. By the time you read the report, the run is gone. {{terminal}} The terminal says what failed. Expected one item in the basket, received zero. It does not say why. {{config}} This lesson collects the evidence while the test runs. A screenshot of the screen at the end. A video of how the page got there. And a trace, which holds every action, every request and every console line, each with its time. {{artefacts}} You will read a trace without its viewer, because a trace is a zip of text files. In one of them, the click on the button comes a second and a half before the script that would have heard it. {{timeline}} Then you attach what the browser said to the report, so an uncaught error arrives beside the failure. {{attach}} You will weigh what all this costs, and keep it only for the tests that fail. {{ci}} And last, a test that compares screenshots, and why a picture taken on one machine fails on another. {{visual}}
